newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES SOAR TO $1.45 BLN IN APR.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES SOAR TO $1.45 BLN IN APR.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) total foreign exchange reserves surged to $1.45 billion at end-April, a post-communist record high, from $853.7 million in March, BNR data showed on Tuesday.
The sharp rise was triggered by purchases of excess dollars from the local interbank market as well as by fresh credits from the International Monetary Fund.
Late last month, the IMF released the first tranche of about $86 million after approving a 13-month $430 million stand-by accord for Romania.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said last month further IMF credits and purchases from the local market would push the BNR reserves to some $2.0 billion in June or July.
In April, the BNR bought large amounts of dollars to prevent the local leu currency from firming due to higher hard currency inflows amid growing foreign interest in Romanian equities.
The leu traded relatively stable near 7,050 to the dollar last month after it had recovered from a plunge to an all-time low of 9,000 in mid-February.
BNR data also showed foreign reserve assets in the banking system rose to $2.88 billion in March from $2.76 billion in February. Figures on April reserve assets were not available.
End-March reserve assets include gold reserves of about 90 tonnes, Special Drawing Rights and hard currency reserves of local banks and of the BNR.
